# `Q-18-5` — Owned Language Has No Runnable Kernel

> The Jupyter engine runs cells in a language, but no installed Jupyter
> kernel declares that language.

## What this means

Quarto gives each `{language}` cell to an engine. The Jupyter engine runs
the cells it is given on a Jupyter kernel, and finds the kernel by the
`language` field of the installed kernelspecs, ignoring case. When no
kernelspec declares the cell's language, Quarto cannot run it.

What happens next depends on the document:

- With an `engine:` list in the front matter, you said which engine runs
  what, so this is an error and the render stops.
- Without one, this is a warning. The cells are left as written and are
  not run, and the render continues.

Cells with `eval: false` never need a kernel and are not reported. A
document that names its kernel (`jupyter: <kernel>`) sends every cell the
Jupyter engine owns to that kernel, so nothing is checked against the
installed kernelspecs.

## How to fix

Install a Jupyter kernel for the language. `jupyter kernelspec list`
shows what Quarto can see. If the kernel is installed in another
environment, run Quarto from a shell where `jupyter` resolves to that
environment, or add its parent directory to `JUPYTER_PATH`.

To run every cell on one multiplexing kernel such as SoS, name it for the
whole document:

```yaml
jupyter: sos
```

If the cell is only meant to be shown, mark it `eval: false`:

````markdown
```{bash}
#| eval: false
ls
```
````

Use `--strict` to make the warning stop the render:

```bash
q2 render --strict
```
